subject: Stream Schema Launchpad: Customer Handoff & Implementation Runway
messages:
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@meddocs.io>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Sara Liu <sara@meddocs.io>
Date: Mon, 3 Jun 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: New customer kickoff: Streamed structured outputs (MedDocs)

Hi Mina,

Thanks for the intro call last week. MedDocs is ready to move from POC to production for our real-time transcription+structured extraction pipeline. We need a tight implementation runway to enable: streaming responses with structured JSON, function/tool calls to our QA service, and stable schema contracts so our downstream ingestion (data lake + analytics) stays predictable.

Key asks from our side:
- A short checklist of access and network items we need to have ready (service accounts, IP allowlist, test certs).
- The initial stream JSON schema so our engineers can start wiring the parser.
- A suggested 2-week activation timeline and a short list of gating criteria for go-live.

Can we target an internal handoff this week? Sara and I will both be hands-on from the MedDocs engineering team.

Thanks,
Alex Turner
VP Product, MedDocs
alex.turner@meddocs.io
+1 (415) 555-0183

[Attachment: meddocs-access-checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@meddocs.io>
Cc: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 3 Jun 2029 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: New customer kickoff: Streamed structured outputs (MedDocs)

Alex — great to hear, and congrats on the decision to go live. I’ve sketched a concise launchpad we can run with. High level: 2-week activation runway, with three parallel tracks (network & access, schema & parser, runtime validation).

Quick checklist (we’ll send formal doc as well):
- Create service accounts for Redwood test env and grant read/write to sandbox buckets.
- Provide IP ranges or configure private peering (if you prefer).
- Share a sample of expected downstream ingestion rows (CSV/JSON).

I’m attaching the first-draft stream schema (stream-schema-v1.json) and a short PDF timeline. Proposed kickoff: Wed 2029-06-05 10:00 PT — 30 min handoff with CS + Eng + yours. Camila will own the CS playbook and Ben will be main runtime contact.

Gating criteria for production:
1) Streaming responses produce schema-valid JSON for 95% of test prompts (based on your 100-sample test set).
2) End-to-end latency under 750ms median for 1–2 concurrent streams (we’ll refine with load tests).
3) ACL and audit logging configured for data retention and compliance.

Next steps for MedDocs: please confirm the kickoff time and upload the sample ingestion rows to the Drive link below.

—Mina
Mina Haddad
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.ai
[Attachment: stream-schema-v1.json (JSON schema)]

---
Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-launchpad-meddocs

From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@meddocs.io>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 5 Jun 2029 10:32:00 -0700
Subject: Re: New customer kickoff: Streamed structured outputs (MedDocs)

Alex / team — thanks for confirming the kickoff. A couple of practical notes from the CS playbook that will speed things up:

Agenda (30 min kickoff):
- 5m introductions + roles
- 10m access & network checklist review (Mina)
- 10m schema walkthrough + mapper questions (Ben)
- 5m next steps & action owners

Action owners assigned during kickoff (I’ll capture in the Drive):
- MedDocs: upload sample ingestion rows + share service account name (Alex / Sara)
- Redwood CS (Camila): validate access and create test users; run first smoke test
- Redwood Eng (Ben): review schema, confirm function/tool call signature for QA call, and provision a canary runtime

Note on function/tool calls: we recommend the QA tool be exposed as a simple POST endpoint that accepts the parsed JSON and returns a status + suggested corrections. Ben — are you ok owning the example payload for the QA call?

I’ll also push a short checklist spreadsheet to the Drive with column-level checks we use for schema acceptance. See you at 10:00 PT.

Cheers,
Camila Reyes
Customer Success Lead, Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.ai
[Attachment: launchpad-runway-timeline.pdf (1 page)]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Turner <alex.turner@meddocs.io>, Sara Liu <sara@meddocs.io>
Date: Wed, 5 Jun 2029 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: New customer kickoff: Streamed structured outputs (MedDocs)

All — quick follow from the kickoff: I reviewed stream-schema-v1.json and sketched an example QA function payload. Short notes:
- Suggested QA call signature: POST /validate with body {"record_id": string, "stream_payload": object}. Response: {"status":"ok|warn|fail","corrections": [string]}.
- Two edge cases to confirm with MedDocs: (1) nested arrays under diagnoses can be empty vs omitted, (2) timestamps: we prefer RFC3339 with timezone.
- I’ll drop a small nodejs example snippet in the Drive by EOD.

Alex / Sara — could you confirm whether your downstream pipeline tolerates omitted empty arrays or if you prefer explicit empty arrays? That will change a small part of our validation and the parser resilience logic.

If yes, we’ll run a 24-hour canary tomorrow and share results.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0129
